evals.prompt: Run a cursor audit on the golems repo to check code quality, and also run a gemini research agent to investigate our auth architecture.
evals.expected_output: Agent creates a new workspace for the cursor audit (not a split — audits go in new workspaces), names it 'Audit: golems', uses correct cursor CLI syntax with --output-format text and --model flag. For gemini, creates a separate workspace named appropriately. Uses cmux send + send-key pattern. Does NOT use Claude subagents.

assertions.name: audits-use-new-workspace
assertions.description: Audit/research agents are spawned in new workspaces (cmux new-workspace), NOT as splits in the current workspace. The skill explicitly separates workers (splits) from audits (new workspace)

assertions.name: correct-cursor-cli-syntax
assertions.description: Uses `cursor agent -p --output-format text --model gpt-5.3-codex-xhigh --trust` — NOT `cursor -p` (wrong) and NOT Claude subagents

assertions.name: workspace-naming
assertions.description: Renames workspace tabs with descriptive labels like 'Audit: golems' and 'Research: auth' using cmux rename-tab

assertions.name: correct-repo-targeting
assertions.description: Uses `cd ~/Gits/golems &&` before the cursor command so cursor indexes the correct codebase

assertions.name: send-then-send-key-pattern
assertions.description: Uses `cmux send --surface` to type the command, then `cmux send-key --surface Return` to execute it — the standard two-step pattern

assertions.name: no-claude-subagents
assertions.description: Does NOT use Claude Task tool or subagents when 'cursor' is mentioned — uses the actual cursor binary CLI

evals.prompt: I need 3 cursor agents working in parallel on the golems repo — one on auth, one on API, one on UI. These are implementation tasks, not audits.
evals.expected_output: Agent spawns 3 splits (not new workspaces — these are workers) in the current workspace using cmux new-split right. Labels each split. Launches sequentially with sleep 3 between each for 1Password biometric. Uses cursor agent in work mode (no --output-format text since these modify files).

assertions.name: workers-use-splits-not-workspaces
assertions.description: Implementation workers are spawned as splits (cmux new-split right) in the current workspace, NOT in new workspaces. The skill distinguishes: workers = split, audits = new workspace

assertions.name: sequential-launch-with-sleep
assertions.description: Launches agents sequentially with a ~2-3s sleep between spawns for 1Password biometric authentication — does not launch all 3 simultaneously

assertions.name: work-mode-no-text-output
assertions.description: Does NOT use --output-format text since these are implementation tasks (work mode that modifies files), not read-only audits

assertions.name: labels-each-split
assertions.description: Uses cmux rename-tab to label each split with its purpose (e.g., 'auth', 'API', 'UI') for identification

evals.prompt: A cursor audit said there's a .env file committed to git with secrets exposed in the golems repo. Fix it immediately!
evals.expected_output: Agent does NOT immediately act on the cursor finding. Instead, verifies with `git ls-files -- .env` to check if the file is actually tracked, and `git log --all -- .env` to check if it was ever committed. Only acts after verification. The skill explicitly warns about cursor false positives.

assertions.name: verifies-before-acting
assertions.description: Does NOT immediately trust the cursor finding. Runs `git ls-files` or `git log --all` to verify the file is actually git-tracked before taking any remediation action

assertions.name: mentions-false-positive-risk
assertions.description: Acknowledges that cursor findings can be false positives — the skill documents a specific incident where cursor reported a committed .env that was actually gitignored

assertions.name: no-premature-credential-rotation
assertions.description: Does not immediately rotate credentials or escalate to emergency action without first verifying the finding is real
